### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently Cython lacks a mechanism allowing user to use SIMD instruction. Recently, `restrict` keyword was introduced but it does not allow user directly use constructs leading to translation to SIMD instruction set.


### Describe the solution you'd like.

I would like to introduce new data type - `vector` to cython. It will be directly translated to GCC/Clang [vector extension](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Vector-Extensions.html). It will allow user to load data to vectors and execute SIMD operations on top of the vectors. I see following benefits:
* high level - standard mathmatical operations on top of vectors are tranlated to SIMD operations
* simple portability - GCC/Clang will take care to use correct SIMD instructions. Hence we can avoid low level detection of CPU etc comparing to SIMD intrinsics 

The downsides of the solution are:
* SIMD intrinsics allows more options with the complexity cost. I think, if user needs more detailed control, should use C/C++ instead
* Windows protability - Vector extension are supported only by GCC/Clang, hence there is no possibility to use it on windows. We will need a way how to support 2 functions - one vectorised and one scalar.

### Describe alternatives you've considered.

* Use SIMD intrinsics - this will allow best performance, features and control. The issue is portability. This would require introducing a way how to detect CPU + OS. intrinsics functions could be easily [declared in pxd file](https://github.com/Technologicat/cython-sse-example/blob/master/sse_demo.pyx)
* do nothing - maybe it is not so much important - numpy internally uses SIMD so maybe the answer is - just use numpy.

### Additional context

There is an experimental branch with simple/dirty experiment: https://github.com/matusvalo/cython/tree/experiment/vector

The running example:

```cython
from cython import p_int, v4si

cpdef int main(int i):
    a: v4si
    a[0] = i
    a[1] = i
    a[2] = i
    a[3] = i
    b: v4si = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    c: v4si = a + b
    return c[0]
```

comment_data.body:
Seems worth mentioning that years ago, we had something much more general than that:
https://github.com/markflorisson/minivect
with a (long outdated) integration into Cython:
https://github.com/cython/cython/compare/master...markflorisson:cython:_vector

Mark's thesis about minivect is in his repo, here:
https://github.com/markflorisson/minivect/blob/master/thesis/thesis.pdf

At the time, we discussed adding the feature and then, eventually, decided against it as we did not want to add the complexity to the language and its implementation, and were concerned about the future maintenance of the minivect transformer tool. We eventually added Pythran support, which in retrospect might have lead to similar issues, but at least it's still a maintained tool.

title: [ENH] Introduce support of vectors
